title: API Contract Drift Detector — Semantic Output Drift & Compatibility Scorecard
creator: Priya Nair
description:
Problem: As we onboard more open models and vendor variants, changes in their tokenization, default sampling, or structured-output behavior create subtle API contract drift. Customers (especially latency-sensitive SaaS buyers) experience silent regressions: increased hallucination rates, changed JSON field ordering/keys, or fewer tokens returned which break downstream pipelines.

Objective: Deliver a lightweight Detector + Compatibility Scorecard that continuously compares a canonical set of synthetically and customer-derived prompts against production model endpoints and emits graded alerts when semantic output drift crosses thresholds. The system should be usable by PMs/SEs to prioritize procurement or fallback actions.

Success metrics: 
- Detect regressions with <24h median detection time for high-volume customers.
- Reduce customer-escaped regressions by 40% in next quarter.
- Provide a per-model compatibility score (0-100) that correlates with engineering triage time (target Spearman rho > 0.5).

Scope (in): 
- Define baseline prompt suites (canonical + 10 high-priority customer prompts).
- Implement lightweight semantic-similarity checks (embedding cosine + schema-aware checks) and output-structure diffs.
- Scorecard UI wireframe in Console and programmatic API for automated routing rules.
- Integration with Alerts (Console / PagerDuty) and rerouting policies (fallback to pinned model).

Scope (out): 
- Full-scale model evaluation lab (bigger performance benchmarks) and expensive adversarial fuzzing — out for MVP.

Approach: 
1) PM to curate initial prompt-suite and acceptance heuristics. 2) Eng to build Detector microservice (small batch replays, embeddings store) and expose score via internal API. 3) Console to display score & recent diffs and provide quick-run on-demand checks. 4) Create playbook mapping score bands to next steps (canary, lock version, escalate to supplier).

Risks & mitigations: 
- False positives from non-actionable variability: mitigate with tunable thresholds and schema-aware checks.
- Cost of continuous checks at scale: start with sampled customers and high-sensitivity tiers, then expand.
- Customer privacy for prompt samples: use hashed prompts and customer opt-in; avoid storing raw PII prompts in Detector storage.

Milestones: 
- 2026-03-01: prompt-suite & heuristics approved by Trust & Safety and 2 SEs.
- 2026-03-15: Eng PoC that runs nightly replay for 5 customer accounts.
- 2026-03-31: Console scorecard wireframe and internal preview.
- 2026-04-07: MVP rollout to Opt-in customers and on-call playbook published.

2026-03-01 Ava Chen (SE): Ran initial suite against 6 open models; found systematic truncation on 2 models for long-context prompts — logged ENG-8421. Notes: truncation increases false-positives for semantic checks, suggested adding prefix/token-count deltas to heuristics.

2026-03-04 Engineering sync (ENG owners: Lara Kim): Agreed PoC will use nightly batched replays and offload embeddings to vector-store (internal). Trade-off: run nightly to reduce cost vs near-real-time for high-value customers. Decided to prioritize nightly for MVP.
2026-03-08 Design review: Console wireframe reviewed by Miguel and Priya; feedback to add 'quick-run' CTA and per-prompt drilldown. Design spec: https://drive.google.com/designs/api-drift-scorecard

2026-03-10 Miguel Ortega: Updated spec with structured-output diff examples and drafted playbook mapping (score 0-40: immediate rollback; 41-70: canary + engineer investigation; 71-100: monitor). Added initial set of customers for opt-in preview (10 accounts).
acceptance_criteria: Detector service ingests canonical prompt-suite and runs nightly replays against configured model endpoints
Scorecard API returns a numeric compatibility score and recent diff artifacts for each model-version
Console preview displays scores, per-prompt diffs, and has Quick-Run button that triggers on-demand check
Playbook documented and on-call runbook linked; routing rules can be configured to fallback when score <= 40
Privacy checks in place (hashed prompts, retention policy) and Trust & Safety sign-off obtained
